run.title: Three White Lights
run.subtitle: Gauntlet Loop build run
run.waveName: Wave 4 — the app is playable; grading the lift and closing the streak guardrail

blockers.title: Twelve blind checks so far, and the pattern is always the same
blockers.body: Every one measured a proxy rather than the claim: a property test whose generator never produced the failing case, a bound the unfixed behaviour already satisfied, a hash standing in for a picture, a BigInt re-derivation checking the formula instead of the digits it printed. None were sloppiness; each was structurally unable to observe what it was written to observe.
blockers.consequence: Mutation testing is now the default ask on every dispatch — break the behaviour, watch the test fail, restore, report the output. It has caught four in the last few hours that reading could not. The harness itself is now in scope for the same treatment: evidence bundles stamp their commit, and the progress page says so when a named screenshot is missing rather than quietly showing nothing.

blockers.title: The app is playable, and the harness that proved it was itself blind
blockers.body: App.tsx imports LiftScreen and a rep can be played in the browser — the day-one Skia spike is gone. But the tool built to prove the lift animates heavier never decoded a pixel: it hashed file bytes and compared probe values produced by the code under test. Copying the light screenshots over the maximal ones, with both manifests untouched, still made it report that the maximal attempt animates heavier. A renderer that drew nothing would have passed it.
blockers.consequence: That is the twelfth check this run that could not fail if the thing it named were deleted, and the worst, because everything downstream trusted it — including a status report I had already given. The heavier-at-maximal claim now rests on a critic's own inspection of the crops, which is a different and real basis: bar bend 3 against 1, strain climbing 0 to 3 against flat 0, ascent 69 ticks against 38. A builder is making the tool decode pixels and adding mutants that freeze the sprite while leaving the bar-path trace live.

blockers.title: Both open design questions decided by the human
blockers.body: Attempt weight: the GDD's "drop down" option is removed — within a lift, attempts repeat or increase, never decrease, and the tension is rewritten accordingly. e1RM: Epley named specifically, one formula, Brzycki banned from the codebase.
blockers.consequence: The meet engine already enforced non-decreasing, so that decision cost no code. The Epley decision did: Brzycki was the fallback past the chart's coverage precisely because Epley steps DOWN there (chart 1.7422w at rep max 16 vs Epley 1.5500w at 16.5). Rather than ship a non-monotonic curve or keep a banned formula, the module now refuses past a 16 effective rep max — a real capability loss, spelled out in its header and enumerated in tests.

blockers.title: Run halted once on the subagent spend limit, now resumed
blockers.body: Six agents were killed mid-flight when the monthly limit was hit: two critics, the e1RM rework, and the fatigue, streak and sprite builders. No usable work was lost — neither partially-started builder had committed anything, and their worktrees were discarded.
blockers.consequence: Dispatch is working again. The queue resumed in priority order: close the e1RM send-back first, then grade the two modules that were merged but never judged. The art and UI half of the run still has not started.

blockers.title: Reference now exists for some bars; four of the five still have no artifact
blockers.body: Five reference files are committed. That unblocks the sprite craft bar, which is being graded against a native-resolution SNES sprite for the first time — every earlier pass reported it unverifiable.
blockers.consequence: The other four previously-unverifiable bars cannot be re-run: the result card, gym art, meet-day sequence and cut-ins are not built yet, so there is nothing to compare. Their references are staged. Two limits remain even then — the meet photos are stills, so meet-day tension's "judge pacing and sound" half stays unverifiable without video, and the scoresheet is a live in-meet attempt board rather than a published federation results sheet.

pieces.name: Foundation
pieces.bar: Not a GDD bar — infrastructure. Must render, screenshot, and test.
pieces.note: Expo + TS strict + vitest + Skia-on-web + Playwright screenshot harness all verified working end to end.

pieces.name: RPE → %1RM table
pieces.bar: Published RPE charts. Binary and testable — critic verifies against source values.
pieces.note: WINS ITS BAR after six rounds. The final critic re-fetched both sources live at the pinned SHAs and confirmed every sampled cell matches the bytes, that the one documented disagreement is real and exactly where the module says it is, that no export remains mutable, that no indexed read can leak undefined past a null check, and that the hot path is unchanged. It named two stale-prose residuals and explicitly said not to spawn a round for them — folded into this touch instead. The chart still cannot be checked against the RTS publication from here, and the module claims no more than that.

pieces.name: e1RM formulas
pieces.bar: Published e1RM formulas. Binary and testable.
pieces.note: THE MATH WINS ITS BAR. The critic verified the Epley divisor against published sources and a pinned third-party implementation, re-fetched both chart fixtures and confirmed every cell the boundary figures depend on, hand-checked all five worked examples and the crossover point, confirmed the curve is strictly increasing across the whole domain and that the refusal fires exactly where the chart’s coverage ends, and found no invented value anywhere. All seven §12.3 conditions clean. Its one finding was a false quotation of CLAUDE.md in the module header — correct that the quote was false, but wrong about how: git history shows the phrase WAS in CLAUDE.md when the builder quoted it, and I removed it two commits later without updating the quotation. My staleness, not a fabrication. Fixed by quoting the rule as it now stands, verified verbatim against the flattened file.

pieces.name: DOTS scoring
pieces.bar: Published DOTS coefficients. Binary and testable.
pieces.note: WINS ITS BAR — the only piece to be graded and pass. All ten coefficients verified by the critic against source bytes it fetched itself from OpenPowerlifting, term order checked by hand two ways. Noted gap: no test pins any DOTS value to anything outside the repo, so a wrong digit at authoring time could not fail the suite.

pieces.name: Meet engine
pieces.bar: Meet structure correctness: order, 3 attempts, non-decreasing weight, best-per-lift total, bomb-out.
pieces.note: Structure WINS ITS BAR. Rework 5 merged: the rules-seal subsystem is gone — four constants, a unique-symbol brand, an error code, an exported check, four call sites, a 41-line essay and nine tests, including the BigInt re-derivation blind to the digits it was meant to check. Rules are now opaque behind a module-private symbol, so the tampering spread does not type-check, and the guard is proven by negative controls that revert it and confirm the directives go unused. meet.ts is 51 lines shorter and has no arithmetic left to get wrong.

pieces.name: Fatigue / readiness
pieces.bar: Plausible game-feel abstraction. No visible fatigue meter (§12.3).
pieces.note: PASSES ITS BAR. The critic had cleared the model and both live §12.3 refusal conditions, re-deriving the daily-vs-intermittent injury comparison by hand rather than taking the claim; what it sent back was two tests that could not fail if the behaviour they named were deleted. Both are now fixed and I re-ran the mutations myself rather than accepting the report: delete the technique-relief term and 1 test fails where 0 did before; delete physio shortening and 2 fail where 0 did. The technique test now pins the exact scaling across six ratings instead of asserting probability > 0, and physio is compared against the same duration roll unaided instead of restating a band the unaided value already satisfied. The third, weaker case was given real content rather than deleted, and the builder proved that by mutation too. Model untouched throughout.

pieces.name: Streak / Recovery Days
pieces.bar: Never punishes daily engagement. Manual token use, hold cap, first-break tutorial.
pieces.note: Runway disclosed and the two overclaims rewritten; wants a re-grade. The offer now carries lastDayStreakCanBeSaved, on RecoveryDayOffer rather than the opening, so it travels through sameOffer — a fabricated offer claiming a longer runway is refused the same way a fabricated lower price is. It is deliberately NOT echoed in the outcome, because after accepting, openDay returns streak-alive which already carries the identical number; the builder asserted that invariance by sweep rather than arguing it, and so left the pay-to-win allowlist unwidened. Its mutation pass is the good kind: inflating the runway by one day fails four tests, and after fixing the vacuous BOUND THAT DOES HOLD sweep it deleted the offer mechanism entirely, confirmed the new guards catch it, then stripped just the seven guard lines and watched the old body pass with the mechanism still gone — proving the pre-fix test was vacuous exactly as the critic described. I verified the one thing the builder flagged as unchecked, since it had been written into the GDD: Duolingo streak freezes are bought in advance, stay equipped until you miss a day, are consumed automatically by the missed day itself, and explicitly cannot be bought retroactively. The claim holds, so the residue really does follow from §4.2 manual use rather than from finiteness. 934 tests, typecheck clean.

pieces.name: Tuning constants
pieces.bar: Every game-feel value a named constant in one place. Enforced by a magic-number audit.

pieces.name: Progression boundary
pieces.bar: No client-authoritative progression writes. Shaped for Edge Functions.
pieces.note: Sent back on the same defect as last round, applied to the other axis — and the file had already fixed that exact pattern twice elsewhere. The critic verified everything else by re-derivation: forging is impossible, spread and Object.assign compile but are INERT because every reader goes through the private symbol, structuredClone and JSON round-trip throw, the confirmed total really is a dots.ts official total with no cast, and the streak wire is coupled to streak.ts rather than duplicating it. It confirmed the money derivation genuinely closes its hole and is not vacuous. The gap: the reach maps are hand-written string literals bound to nothing, and they are the OPERAND of both pay-to-win disjointness assertions. Rename a fact and the allowlist and protected-concerns list are both forced to update, but the reach map still names the old key and still compiles — so the assertion passes BY SPELLING, for the wrong reason, and the next author copying that stale row into a purchase-tagged kind sails through. The non-vacuity guards cannot see it, because a drifted union is still non-empty; it just refers to nothing. That contradicts the header's own claim to cover the case where a guard survives deletion of the thing it guards. I verified the binding is a pure addition — it compiles against the current values — so nothing needs redesigning. The critic also caught the money residual understating itself: keyof is top-level only, so a nested store envelope escapes too, not just a promo code.

pieces.name: Lift input mechanic
pieces.bar: The lift must feel good (GDD pillar 1).
pieces.note: SENT BACK, and the finding is the worst kind this run has produced: the verification tool is itself blind. tools/verify-lift-shots.mjs prints that the maximal attempt animates heavier without ever decoding a pixel — it sha256s file bytes and otherwise compares probe values that come from the app under test. I ran the critic's exploit: copy the light PNGs over the maximal ones, leave both manifests untouched, and it still reports OK, both sequences are semantically distinct and the maximal one animates heavier, over two byte-identical sets of pictures. A renderer that drew nothing would pass it. Its within-sequence check is vacuous too, because the hashed region is the whole canvas including the bar-path trace, which differs at every tick regardless of what the sprite does. So the 9 of 9 and 8 of 9 figures I reported are not backed by what I ran, and I have corrected that. What is genuinely established is the critic's OWN inspection of the crops: bar bend 3 against 1, strain climbing 0 to 3 against flat 0 for the whole light rep, forward drift 3.77px against 0.97px, ascent 69 ticks against 38, and a trace that stalls and reverses against a plumb line. Two more: the drive cue re-arms after its window closes, so the comment saying it arms the first time is false and the win rates justifying the default load describe a game the player is not playing; and the default of 0.88 still lets an undriven ideal-depth rep reach lockout, so the drive decides grind-vs-good-lift and never make-vs-miss — the same objection used to reject 0.75. My evidence bundle was also stale, which was my error; regenerated.

pieces.name: Lifter sprites & animation
pieces.bar: Blind A/B against real 16-bit sprite work — NOW GRADEABLE, reference committed.
pieces.note: HEAVINESS WON OUTRIGHT, and the lower body is fixed — but the same defect turned out to be sitting one level up. The critic confirmed on current post-fix frames that maximal runs brace-to-lockout in 139 ticks against light's 81, ascent 68 against 37, stall 4 against 0, forward lean peaking 3.77px against 0.97, strain and pitch both reaching rung 3 while light never leaves 0. It confirmed the bent-leg inversion that took two rounds is genuinely closed, and that the previous builder was right to refuse the shin rotation. What it found: the near-black keyline fix was applied below the belt and DELIBERATELY withheld above it, with a comment in palette.ts calling the dark breaks anatomical work. The pixels refuse that — I looked myself, and against the native SNES reference both wrestlers carry their brightest flesh on the arms while ours are the darkest thing on the figure. The blind A/B inverts: we have bright legs and black arms, the reference has the reverse. It is structural, a 5px limb of which two columns are outline ring and one is shadow, doubled where the capsules meet at the elbow — which is also why the hands never resolve, since roughly six fill pixels remain. Fifteenth blind check, and a neatly directional one: the near-black bound is computed on the LOWER half only, and the single upper-over-lower assertion is a ratio CAP, which a darker upper body satisfies more easily rather than less. The bound points the wrong way.

pieces.name: Result card
pieces.bar: Would a competitive lifter believe ours is real? vs. real federation sheets.
pieces.note: Dispatched. GDD §6.5 calls the shareable card the strongest organic growth lever in the game, and its §12.2 bar is a blind A/B against real federation result sheets — would a competitive lifter believe ours is real. The builder is briefed hard on the reference limit: the committed scoresheet image is a LIVE in-meet attempt board, not a published results sheet, so it cannot supply placings, DOTS columns or total conventions. It must cite real sources or state plainly which conventions it invented, and a critic will check exactly that. It consumes meet.ts and dots.ts read-only, and a bombed lifter has to render honestly — attempts and marks shown, no total, no DOTS, never a zero.

pieces.name: Cross-module inconsistency (found, unfixed)
pieces.bar: The four modes must feel like one game — the smoothing-pass concern.
pieces.note: Prose fixed and the blind test replaced; ready for a re-grade. The builder reproduced the leak before writing a word about it — 0.6362511777452804 out of a 1kg mint, formatting as 229.05 for a bombed lifter — and then found a SECOND route I had not asked about and would not have caught: Object.getOwnPropertySymbols(c) names the private key at runtime, so module-private is a fact about typechecking, not about the object. It disclosed that too rather than leaving the phrase implicitly denying it. It did both halves of the test fix: renamed the name-grep to say it is only a name scan, AND added a describe block that executes the route for real. Six mutants all bite, including closing the leak (24 of 128 fail) and restoring the false sentence. The diagnostic it recorded is the point of the whole exercise — under the leak-closing mutation the renamed grep still reports green, so the blindness is now labelled rather than relied on. It also flagged honestly that it did not audit every remaining sentence in a 980-line header for the same defect class, and that a cold critic is the right check for that.
